answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards, then slash that bond when fraud is proven through an auditable dispute process. Rewards can scale with a bond’s age and successful work, so creating many fresh identities does not instantly multiply influence. A yarrow, lotus, or sparrow agent faces the same rule: to fake a crowd, the attacker must lock up capital across identities and risk losing it, making Sybil attacks costly rather than merely requiring more accounts.
